chunks: The simile of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain which grew seven ears, each ear containing a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of spending wealth in the way of God in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the 'Verse of Charity' (Ayat al-Zakah), employs the agricultural metaphor of a single grain yielding seventyfold to illustrate the exponential spiritual return of voluntary spending (Sadaqah) in Shia exegesis. It underscores that while the multiplier is vast, the ultimate expansion of reward remains contingent upon God’s will (Yashau), reflecting His infinite generosity (Was') and omniscience ('Alim).
